notes: Summary: Large omnichannel retailer evaluating Redwood Dedicated for real-time personalization + chat. POC ran Nov->Feb; stalled due to performance gap vs customer's target p95 for streaming responses.
POC setup: 3-node Dedicated pool (gpus: A100s), pinned model: llama-like 34B q4 variant in Redwood catalog, sequence window 2048, token streaming enabled, KV cache warming used.

Metrics observed: target p95 end-to-end for streaming response <300ms (interactive UI requirement). Measured p95 ~950ms for first-byte streaming; tail worse under load (1.2s) on us-east region. Throughput OK for batch ranking but not for low-latency interactive flows.

Root cause analysis from infra: streaming chunk latency dominated by repeated kernel launches and network serialization when KV cache misses occurred. Attempted fixes: adjusted batching, disabled prefix caching for some routes, tuned socket buffer sizes — marginal gains only.
Customer quote (CTO): 'Great accuracy but we can't compromise on perceived latency. FastServe gave us a demo at 260ms p95 in our infra.' — supports why losing to competitor.

Security: heavy requirements — SSO (SAML), on-prem cert rotation, audit_logging retention 7yrs. Security review open; SEC-452 ticket for KMS integration questions. They require proof-of-concept for HSM/KMS flow before procurement.
